preconditions.expression: n >= 2 and m >= n - 1 and m <= 10**6
preconditions.description: The graph has at least 2 destinations and at least n-1 corridors (connected), with no more than 10^6 corridors.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b and 0 <= e <= 10**9 for a, b, e in corridors)
preconditions.description: Each corridor connects two distinct destinations (1 ≤ a, b ≤ n, a ≠ b) with a non-negative energy (0 ≤ e ≤ 10^9).
The input contains exactly m corridors, where m is the first input line.

preconditions.expression: all(a != b for a, b, _ in corridors)
preconditions.description: No pair of destinations {a, b} appears more than once in the input.
The graph is connected, meaning there is a path between any two destinations using the given corridors.

postconditions.expression: E_max == max(e for e in range(0, 10**9 + 1) if exists_mst_with_c1(corridors, e, c1))
postconditions.description: The output E_max is the maximum energy e ≤ 10^9 such that the first corridor (c1) belongs to at least one minimum spanning tree (MST) of the graph when its energy is set to e.

postconditions.expression: E_max == 0 or (E_max > 0 and exists_mst_with_c1(corridors, E_max, c1))
postconditions.description: If E_max is 0, it means the first corridor cannot be part of any MST when its energy is 0. Otherwise, there exists at least one MST that includes the first corridor when its energy is set to E_max.
For any energy e > E_max, the first corridor does not belong to any MST of the graph when its energy is set to e.
